blogTitle: AMV LOG: est. time remaining 6 hours 41 minutes (it said 4 minutes)
about: hi. andy. i make anime music videos (amvs) in windows movie maker on the family computer in the basement. i capture the episodes with hypercam 2, which is the unregistered version, which means every video i've ever made has a little red 'Unregistered HyperCam 2' in the top left corner. 31 videos. 31 corners. people ask if i can take it off. the registration is $39.95. i have $31.40 in a pringles can. a 3 minute video renders for 6 hours 40 minutes, so i don't make a video, i make a decision about my evening. the computer is also my mom's (tuesdays: taxes) and my sister's (4 to 5: neopets), so every render has to survive both. my best one is naruto set to linkin park. i know. they all are. it's the formula.
aboutMore: things i'm good at: cutting on the drum hit (frame perfect, i've watched 'the hit' 214 times at quarter speed), finding the one clip where the guy turns around dramatically, being the guy at the park with the camcorder when ben trains, rendering at 3 AM when the dryer is off and the house is quiet. things i'm bad at: registering things. i've been 'about to register' since march. every time the can gets close, somebody needs a video.
meet: who i'd like to meet: the person at the hypercam company, to ask if he'd take $31.40 and the pringles can (i'd throw in the pringles). whoever animated the breaking the habit video, because it's an anime video that got a budget and i think about it every day. usagi, so i can explain 2:14 of the club recap (it's banana. it's always banana). and whoever invented the 'est. time remaining' bar, to ask if it has ever once been right.

interests.General: making amvs (31), rendering (6h 40m per 3 min), screen capture (unregistered), the pringles can fund ($31.40), cutting on the drum hit, being the camera guy, anime club (videographer, unpaid, it's still a title), watching one clip 214 times, power strips (the good kind)

blog.title: why the watermark stays (a pringles can story)
blog.body: people ask why i don't just take it off. here's the math. hypercam registration: $39.95. in march i started a pringles can. by june i had $22 (lawn money, one birthday card from my aunt). then ben's nana needed a birthday disc and a card, so $17. then more lawn, $26. then devon needed 10 copies for the shop and blank discs are not free, so $21. by august it was $31.40 and i was $8.55 away. $8.55 is one pizza. since then it's been a loop: i get to $36, somebody needs a video, it's $31.40 again. the can has seen things. so it's not that i can't afford it. it's that every time i get close, somebody needs a video. and i've decided that when you can pick between a corner of the screen and a person, you pick the person. the corner can wait. it's red. it's unregistered. it's mine.

blog.title: a beginner's guide to cutting on the drum hit
blog.body: step 1: find the hit. it's the drum part where the song goes from quiet to loud. in the song i'm using it's at 0:43. step 2: find the clip. it has to be the guy turning around. or a sword. or rain. i'm not picky, i'm just specific. step 3: line them up at quarter speed. i watched it 214 times. i'm serious. that's not a joke, that's a number i kept. step 4: render. 6 hours 40 minutes. do not touch the computer. do not breathe near the computer. do not let your sister use the computer. step 5: go to sleep. step 6: wake up and it's at 62%. that's fine. that's the process. step 7: it finishes at 3 AM and you watch it with the sound low, in the dark, in the basement, next to the dryer. and the guy turns around. exactly on the hit. and for 4 seconds the whole thing looks like it was always supposed to happen. that's the whole job. it's like friendship but for a drum.
